effects: The signer pays msg.value in FLR. It must equal the stored reservationFee or the call reverts.
The fee is forwarded to reservationFeeRecipient, an address read from storage.
A new minting-tag NFT (id = nextAvailableTag) is minted to the signer. Its minting recipient is set to the signer and its executor is cleared.
formats.shown: The screen says "reserve minting tag" and shows the native value as 'Reservation Fee' (e.g. 1 FLR).

findings.title: reserve(): the fee recipient comes from storage and is not shown.
findings.evidence: MintingTagManager.sol reserve(): Transfers.transferNAT(reservationFeeRecipient, msg.value). Only @.value 'Reservation Fee' is displayed.
findings.fix: None possible. The fee going to the protocol treasury is what the purchase implies.

findings.title: reserve(): the test sends 1 FLR, but the fee was set to 100 FLR at deployment, so the call may revert.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json value 1000000000000000000. The proxy constructor args in meta.json set _reservationFee 100000000000000000000. reserve() requires msg.value == reservationFee.
findings.fix: Use the current on-chain reservationFee as the test value.

findings.title: reserve(): the intent does not say the signer receives a tag NFT whose id is set by the contract.
findings.evidence: _reserve(): mintingTag = nextAvailableTag; _safeMint(_to, mintingTag). The intent is "reserve minting tag".
findings.fix: Optionally say "Pay fee to reserve a new FXRP minting tag (NFT)".

effects: Only the tag owner can call this. It sets the address that receives FXRP minted with this tag to _recipient (non-zero), until the tag is transferred.
formats.shown: The screen says "set mint recipient" and shows the Tag Id raw and the Recipient address.

findings.title: setMintingRecipient: the intent does not say that future FXRP mints for this tag go to this address.
findings.evidence: _setRecipient(): tag.recipient = _recipient. The intent is "set mint recipient" and the label is 'Recipient'.
findings.fix: Use intent "Send FXRP minted with this tag to" and an interpolatedIntent such as "Send FXRP minted with tag {_mintingTag} to {_recipient}".

findings.title: setMintingRecipient: the addressName types eoa/wallet are narrower than the code allows; any non-zero address is accepted.
findings.evidence: setMintingRecipient(): only require(_recipient != address(0)). The descriptor has params.types ["eoa","wallet"].
findings.fix: Add "contract" to the types or drop the restriction.

effects: Only the tag owner can call this. It schedules _executor as the only address allowed to execute direct mintings with this tag; zero means anyone can.
The change takes effect after executorChangeAfterSeconds, a value from storage. Until then the old executor stays active.
If a change is pending and _executor equals the currently active executor, the pending change is cancelled.
formats.shown: The screen says "Set mint executor (delayed)" and shows the Tag Id raw and the executor address labeled 'Executor (zero = anyone)'.

findings.title: setAllowedExecutor: the length of the cooldown is in storage and is not shown.
findings.evidence: _setExecutor(): allowedExecutorActiveAfterTs = block.timestamp + executorChangeAfterSeconds. The intent only says "(delayed)".

findings.title: setAllowedExecutor: the addressName types eoa/wallet are narrower than the code allows; the executor can be any address, contracts included.
findings.evidence: setAllowedExecutor() puts no restriction on _executor. The descriptor has params.types ["eoa","wallet"].
findings.fix: Add "contract" to the types or drop the restriction.

effects: The tag NFT moves from the signer to _to. There is no ERC721Receiver check.
The tag's minting recipient is reset to _to.
The allowed executor, and any pending executor change, are cleared immediately.
formats.shown: The screen says "Transfer minting tag, reset settings" and shows the To address and the Tag Id raw.

findings.title: transfer: the addressName types eoa/wallet are narrower than the code allows; _to can be a contract.
findings.evidence: transfer(): _transfer(msg.sender, _to, _mintingTag) has no receiver check. The descriptor has params.types ["eoa","wallet"].
findings.fix: Add "contract" to the types or drop the restriction.

findings.title: transfer: "reset settings" does not say the recipient becomes the new owner and the executor is cleared.
findings.evidence: _afterTokenTransfer(): _setRecipient(id, _to); _clearExecutor(id). The intent is "Transfer minting tag, reset settings".
findings.fix: Optionally: "Transfer minting tag {_mintingTag} to {_to}; recipient and executor reset".

findings.title: Inherited ERC721 approve/setApprovalForAll/transferFrom have no formats, though they move or grant rights over tags.
findings.evidence: MintingTagManager is ERC721EnumerableUpgradeable. display.formats lists only reserve, setMintingRecipient, setAllowedExecutor and transfer.
findings.fix: Consider adding formats for approve, setApprovalForAll, transferFrom and safeTransferFrom.
